amendment_after_failed_validation: The first execution failed its positive-covariance assertion because the +6.7% frequency sensor mimic required |cross covariance| greater than noise variance at two lags. Before accepting results, that case alone was replaced by +2.9%, which satisfies the analytic positivity condition. The failure, replacement reason, and fact that other printed outcomes were not used for retuning are retained here. All other scenarios, allocations, tests and thresholds are unchanged.
scope: Matched-lag paired sensor calibration for separating Gaussian sensor covariance from thermal dynamics in finite independent-pair experiments
cost_rule: A dynamic pair or noise-only calibration pair costs two readings. An isolated calibration observation costs one. Calibration reading allocation is floor(B*fraction); paired counts are rounded down to an equal multiple of lag count, dynamic pairs to an even equal multiple for split tests. Unused readings and wait-cost proxy are reported.
isolated_rule: Isolated zero-reference readings estimate one common sensor variance and assume zero within-pair error covariance. Exact chi-square interval has beta error. This mode cannot observe sensor correlations.
paired_rule: Noise-only pairs use the same lags and acquisition order as dynamic pairs. Separate plus/minus noise-coordinate variances receive simultaneous exact chi-square intervals with total beta error. No equality across coordinates or lags is assumed in the physical-family test.
physical_moment_rule: Dynamic plus/minus coordinate chi-square intervals use total alpha_dynamic across all two-sided lag-coordinate statements. A candidate survives when its required noise-coordinate variances intersect calibration intervals. Physical-family rejection requires all three candidates to fail.
split_rule: An arbitrary zero-mean Gaussian fit from train halves is scored on test halves. The null denominator independently maximizes each lag-coordinate variance over calibration-allowed bounds, upper-bounding the physical null likelihood. Threshold is 1/alpha_dynamic.
sensor_alarm: Calibration rejects the nominal independent sensor covariance when nominal noise variance is outside any simultaneous coordinate interval. Isolated mode only checks nominal marginal variance. No alarm exists without calibration.
error_control: With valid transfer, calibrated physical-family methods have rejection probability at most alpha_dynamic+beta=0.025 for an exact physical candidate. Paired sensor alarm has probability at most beta under nominal independent noise. Separate claims do not validate an unadjusted combined rejection rule.
holdout: Fresh decay parameters 0.145 and 0.255, amended frequency shift +2.9 percent, noise SD 0.52, and paired-calibration allocations. The schedule is intentionally inherited because it defines the ambiguity to resolve. No valid-run outcomes may retune thresholds or allocations.
interpretation: Attribution is conditional on calibration transfer and the Gaussian independent-trial model. Exact dynamic-law twins permit a direct attribution comparison but are constructed controls, not evidence about prevalence in real instruments.
limits: Known equilibrium variance, stiffness and temperature; zero means; independent fresh trials; calibration pairs available at matching lags; no uninterrupted stationary colored-noise process, nonlinear dynamics, unknown memory, hardware data, or universal response certificate.
